notes: All hexadecimal is lower case. JSON documents are given as strings; hashes and signatures cover their exact bytes.
Bitcoin only: no case names another asset, the test payment method, or a conversion from another asset.
source names the upstream file and the JSON path of each case; hand_written cases give the rule they follow in basis.
The keys are published test values and must never hold funds.

Members added to upstream cases, naming inputs the checker needs: `recipient_app` (messages), `natural_key_parts` (record_keys), `name`, `identity`, `counterparty`, `acceptance_message` and `record_key_case` (initial_ledger), `name` (compaction). Messages signed again here carry `base`, the upstream message they change.

keys.description: The fixed test keys. Each secret is BLAKE3(seed_prefix + seed label), a 32-byte Ed25519 seed; the public key, Pubky ID (z-base-32), App ID (first 16 bytes of BLAKE3 of the signing key, z-base-32), Switch root derive("pubky-switch/v1/scope-root", secret) and naming key derive("pubky-switch/v1/naming", root) follow from it. These keys are published test values and must never hold funds.

certificates.description: Each Paykit app's certificate, signed by its identity key. Every verifier, the Switch's and Paykit's, accepts each.

executor_certificates.description: Spec 3.1, wire 3.1 and 3.3: the executor's certificate. paykit_allowance_execute requires paykit_allowance, paykit_pay and paykit_contacts, so that every executor reads the deny list. accepted is Paykit's own executor certificate, which the executor grant of this file carries: the executor's certificate of this file's certificates, which holds paykit_contacts. refused is that certificate with paykit_contacts removed from its scopes, so that it holds paykit_allowance_execute without paykit_contacts, and the permissions its scopes need, signed again by alice's identity key: the switch takes it (switch_accepts), and Paykit's verifiers refuse it. reason is paykit-lib's wording at a Paykit verifier.

refused.reason: invalid: paykit_allowance_execute requires paykit_allowance, paykit_pay and paykit_contacts

messages.description: Every message kind as sent in v0.2 (Switch wire 4.5, wire 4): the exact JSON bytes, their BLAKE3 hash (refs, request hash), the sender app's signature over lp("pubky-switch/v1/msg", recipient identity, JSON), and the signed plaintext layout sender app ID (16) | signature (64) | u32_be(JSON length) | JSON, before zero padding.

policies.description: Wire 1.5, Switch wire 1.5: the policies of Paykit's collections, each with its read scope, its write scopes and its policy hash, hash(lp("pubky-switch/v1/policy", read_scope, u64(n), write_scope_1, ..., write_scope_n)), hashed_bytes_hex being the bytes hashed: the fixed policy of each collection, by its name, permanent policies use the permanent-policy label and append their generation as a u64, or zero for a null generation, and, last, payee_activity's policy for a request labelled shop1.

record_keys.description: Wire 1.5, Switch wire 1.5: the record keys of Paykit's natural keys, each in its collection under its policy, blinded with the naming key of the identity whose switch holds it (identity, keys.json): natural_key (and natural_key_hex) is the natural key, blinded_natural_key its blind, derive("pubky-switch/v1/name", naming_key, natural_key), key_material_hex the input of the record key, lp(collection, blinded_natural_key, policy_hash), and record_key derive("pubky-switch/v1/record", collection, blinded_natural_key, policy_hash). The request hashes are those of messages.json's payment_request, payment_request_recurring (its February period, 1772236800) and payment_request_labelled, whose payee record is under the policy of its label shop1. The last is the settlements bucket of the bitcoin-txid settlement of the payment without a request, its settlement_id, held at bob's switch: settlement_tag_input_hex is lp(settlement ID), blinded_settlement_tag_input its blind, settlement_tag_hex the settlement's tag, derive("paykit/v1/settlement", "tag", blinded_settlement_tag_input), bucket u16_be(tag[0..2]) >> 6, mark_settlement_tag_hex bytes 2 to 13 of the tag, which its mark stores, and natural_key lp(u64(bucket)); occurrence_tag_hex is the first 8 bytes of derive("paykit/v1/settlement", "occurrence", occurrence_blinded_natural_key), the blind of the natural key of the occurrence it was credited to, bob's payee record of that payment. natural_key_parts names the parts of the natural key's lp() (wire 1.5 Natural keys).

usage.description: Allowance usage (wire 5.5, spec 8.3 with specs/allowances.md): for every period limit the amount and count of counted entries in the period containing t (anchored) or with t < at + 60 s + L (rolling), the lifetime amount including compacted totals, and entry counts reserved, spent and released. A ledger or claim done, or a validated payer proof, spends. Open and unknown claims reserve entries without an outcome. Every failed attempt spends immediately, whoever wrote the failure, while its claim remains and after it is gone. Only durable journal evidence bound to the attempt proving it ended before the payment method's call and can never dispatch releases it; a restored journal, a reported failure or user confirmation alone is insufficient. Done or a paid proof overrides release. An entry without an outcome whose claim is gone spends. Compacted totals.failed items use the same rule for lifetime usage. Candidates are checked against every limit; refused_by names the first limit that refuses. failure_evidence holds pure counting inputs: evidence means already validated local journal and payer-proof evidence, not a shared record member; Callers must bind it to the attempt, obligation, Allowance, amount, asset and owner. Its compacted cases replace the entry with one totals.failed item. period_limit_spellings checks duplicate terms by wire spelling; period_limit_members checks required members. compaction/successors checks which newer ledger versions a reader holding an older one accepts after a compaction it didn't see.

outcomes: open and unknown reserve; failed attempts spend; missing claims spend
rolling 7 days: an entry counts until at + 60 s + 7 days
rolling 7 days: the entry has left the window
failures by either app spend; done overrides a failed ledger outcome
compacted failed attempts spend while claims remain and after they are gone
never dispatched, failed ledger, claim gone
compacted paid proof overrides never dispatched
compacted done claim overrides never dispatched

successors.description: Wire 5.5 From one version to the next, spec 8.3: a reader holds held, written at service time held_time, and reads newer, written at newer_time, which no longer lists a held entry. newer counts that entry in its totals, as a compaction writes it. The reader accepts newer when the entry's at + longest period + 60 s was before some service time from held_time to newer_time, the longest period taken at that time, so an anchored month or year limit's entry compacted in a shorter period is accepted in a version written in a longer one. A held_time after newer_time judges at newer_time alone. accepted is the verdict.

cases.name: monthly: compacted at February's end, written in March
monthly: held from the newer write's time, judged in March alone
monthly: held from after the newer write's time, judged at newer_time alone
monthly: no time from held_time to newer_time could compact the entry
yearly: compacted at 2027's end, written in leap year 2028
yearly: held from the newer write's time, judged in 2028 alone
